item.title: Friendship bracelet seeking greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: An anomalous bracelet which removes the wearers ability to experience any and all negative emotions. This bracelet then compels its wearer to create "friendship bracelets" out of available materials and attempts to convince others to wear these bracelets. the original bracelet changes size in order to always fit its wearer, the other bracelets created by an affected person have all the same effects excluding this one.

Central Narrative: The story will be told through an interview log of an agent who was sent as part of a pair to investigate a quickly growing cult. The cult was in possession of the original bracelet and all of its members were wearing other instances. The agent will have been tortured, along with their partner dying to the torture, and was recovered along with the SCP when an MTF was deployed.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The story is an exploration of the implications of a person (or group of people) having a single goal that consumes their life. This exploration is diversified by the individuals not having negative emotions (which lead to morals) to "hold them back".

Additional Notes: I have a draft of the SCP article, and would like tweaks before I write the interview.

item.title: Typowriter (Seeking Greenlight/Critiques or Edits)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: Highly powerful reality bender manifesting in the form of a common typewriter. The typewriter will essentially create "transcripts" of nearby media, although it often makes typos. If a typo happens to create a sentence in the transcript that grammatically makes sense, it will become reality. It runs forever and will make increasingly more typos on a transcript if the same piece of media is shown to it multiple times.

Central Narrative: I plan for this to be an SCP that has been in containment for awhile, however without any reliable containment procedures. There will be an extensive list of research notes and observations about the operations of SCP XXXX. The main "narrative" stems from a recovered journal. The SCP is contained by singing up 4 unwitting rural towns to use their local news stations, newspapers, and radio broadcasts for SCP XXXX. Although MTFs patrol all 4 towns constantly, one woman begins to keep a journal of all the weird alterations that happen, so she can be sure she isn't going crazy (as the towns are frequently amnestizied due to the SCP)

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Completely random reality bender that is able to warp anything by writing a typo

Additional Notes: The reality anchors do not work on this SCP, in actuality because it kills some of the fun associated with it. I think a decent theory within the narrative as to why this is so is that SCP XXXX is a recovered byproduct of SCP 3812 (SCP-3812)

item.title: Greenlight Concept - Article - Horror / History -Related to Sarkicism & CotBG
item.description: Seeking review of concept for an SCP article.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking review of concept for an SCP article. Tried this out about nine years ago, did bad, and want to give it another go having read a lot more of the material and matured as a writer/person.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up a lot of space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror & History

Page Layout (Optional): Standard in-depth containment procedure, followed by a retrieval log and accompanied by a brief test log with two or three addenda related to the nature of the SCP. I don't want to perform anything out of the ordinary format-wise with it being my first entry, but a timeline of the SCP's apprehension by groups of interest may be relevant.

Elevator Pitch:

A forest-spirit/lesser goddess of creation and fertility that asexually births creatures based
upon what she consumes is captured by the Church of the Broken God, and turned into a weapon to convert organic material into inorganic material. They lose her, and she exchanges hands between organizations for hundreds of years before ending up in foundation custody totally unrecognizable to what she once was, with a sinister corruption of her godly ability.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative:

Following the first war of the Flesh, Cyrus the Great founded a covenant to search the world for a new means to defeat the Sarkic threat. This group set out, with generations passing before eventually finding a minor fertility goddess unique in her ability to produce life asexually and rapidly by consuming organic matter. They captured her, but became indoctrinated by the Church of the Broken God over time, and augmented her heavily. She would eventually escape with the aid of a man enamored with her, and sire a child with him, the location of which is unknown but she is believed to be endowed with the same ability. Over time different organizations got ahold of the spirit and altered her repeatedly to suit their needs or designs with her now bordering on unrecognizable as herself.

Her modern iteration is a mess of added mechanical and organic apertures both internal and external that have removed her god-like beauty to some extent. Her mistreatment by mankind has jaded her to the point of being predatory, and resulted in her fractured psyche turning to exploitation and predation of mankind through producing her unique offspring. Organic material she consumed is now converted into mechanically augmented horrors when she births them, and vice versa.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:

The concept of the perversion of sexuality, creation, and birth for the purpose of furthering an agenda is enticing and provocative. Taking an earthly minor-goddess of creation and weaponizing her between the Sarkites and Mekhanites and turning her into a cog in the war machine between them serves as a potent analogy for the corruption of life and nature to fit the destruction of it, while sympathizing the reader to a malignant goddess that was once benign and pure.

Additional Notes: I believe I've thought this through reasonably well, but am making space to afford the word count. Some gaps in reasoning are apparent here that I don't have space to explain.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

+ show block

Central Narrative: A child is playing under a blanket fort with his parents. After his father shows him how to make shadow puppets with a flashlight and his hands, the child follows suit. The shadows he makes are living, and proceed to "devour" his parents. After not seeing the family leave their house for a while, police are called to the scene. After they enter, gunshots are heard, and then shadows dart around the house. A junior researcher who lives nearby calls in the situation and Foundation agents contain the child. The junior researcher is assigned to the SCP and tries to calm him down, though he knows what the Foundation might do to the child.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The story of an innocent child doing normal things that becomes under the control of the cold and calculating Foundation.

However, they do not terminate him at the end of the month and make him a SCP because he knows stuff only an 05 knows.

+ show block
– hide block

Hook/Attention-Grabber: At the end of the SCP in an addendum, the site director says something like, "We do not know for certain that he is an 05 despite him having classified information. He could be an attempt at infiltration by a GoI, a Class-D who anomalously got his hands on classified information and is attempting to avoid end-of-the-month termination. Maybe he actually is 05-14 and was placed as a Class-D. We really do not know anything about him, and it is much safer to simply contain him than to blindly trust any assumptions. Rest assured, we are investigating this."

As in, maybe some guard slips him a note saying that he believes him, and intends to break him out/investigate it himself. Also, apologies for any mistakes I make, this is my first post ever on the site and I really want to start writing an article after lurking for a couple of years.

item.title: A multidimensional book about records
item.description: A book containing all the records
item.content:encoded:
A book containing all the records set by any entity in any dimension in all of existence. (SCP version of Guinness world records but a multiversal edition)

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Tale

Genre: Drama/Emotional, Comedy,

Page Layout: Standard

Elevator Pitch: The vehement struggle of a researcher coming to terms with the "record" his father holds.

Central Narrative: A researcher is tasked to read through the book containing countless records. Through fan post/mails send from all over the universes, he comes to learn that his idol, his father, is not the man he had imagined him to be. The book itself has no other anomalous qualities then depicting the records.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I think that the premise, of a record book in a world full of extremes, is an interesting idea and something which would draw a lot of attention, provided it is done in a sufficient manner. Many parallels to existing SCPs could be drawn as well. The conflict with the unspeakable atrocity the father might have committed should serve as the main point of interest.

-Whatever crime the father has committed will not be mentioned-

After a lengthy discussion on the critters forum, I came to the conclusion, that this idea is better suited for a tale. It is just a revisited idea of an older idea of mine here is a link to it http://www.scpwiki.com/forum/t-13137282/scp-idea-a-multidimensional-book-about-records

And this is a modernized version of the first thread I had written about the tale idea. Back then, the idea was not fleshed out enough. link http://www.scpwiki.com/forum/t-13675691/a-multidimensional-book-about-records#post-4759034

I do hope that it now is better suited for the said endeavour.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight
item.description: Tale about SCP-745 ("Headlights") from the point of view of an MTF operative
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Tale (draft available)

Page Layout: Short story, simple page

Elevator Pitch: An MTF operative recounts their last night on assignment with SCP-745.

Central Narrative: SCP-745 has long been contained, so years of uneventful duty shifts have resulted in a culture of complacency. One night that boredom is broken by strange occurrences among the specimens, and the team tries make sense of the situation while responding with limited resources and little support.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Wanting to express a sense of realism through a down-to-earth look at the MTF team- a lackluster assignment, and one member's first-person recollections of the events. Also, those events are never really explained, and much is left to be implied, sparking the reader's imagination (we only know what the "author" experienced).

Additional Notes: I've always thought the 745 story has lots of potential for lore-building. Additionally, it's a good place to explore the human factor in that countless containment procedures call for round-the-clock security. They're highly competent professionals, but they're still human beings. It takes a lot to stay vigilant, and one can't be "on alert" indefinitely. How does one respond when suddenly called upon to act?

item.title: Greenlight time?
item.description: The indigenous American Coyote character escapes
item.content:encoded:
The indigenous American Coyote character escapes to his own metanarrative properties, and the Foundation seeks to stop him from spreading to other folklore.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Mostly an exploration of a cool idea

Page Layout: Bog-standard SCP format

Elevator Pitch: The set of Indigenous American stories about Coyote are an anomalous set of living narrative and metanarrative characteristics, which the Foundation worries might "jump" into other contemporary narratives. "Coyote" fools the Foundation and involves the Chaos Insurgency

Central Narrative: There is definitely a plot to this, but I hope you'll find it interesting enough to warrant such a big explanation:

+ show block
– hide block

A culture's practices and beliefs determine its stories, right? But what if the stories start to have a mind (or agenda) of their own? A Foundation anthropologist reports that the set of stories about Coyote acts differently from any other set of stories about a character (indigenous or otherwise); specifically, the stories and the overall set itself shares Coyote's characteristics, as well as some instinct for self preservation and an unknown degree of sapience. This worries the Foundation, who are concerned about what would happen if Coyote discovers how to (or maybe just decides to) jump into other contemporary narrative-sets. They have no idea what will happen in that scenario.

A year later, Foundation web-sweeper bots detect a set of movie concepts, novel plots, and fanfiction arcs, many involving birds of some kind, which overall "behaved like a narrative animal, but with more personality", similarly to the Coyote set. The foundation at first classifies this as a new, similar SCP, but the anthropologist later realizes that it is in fact a containment breach, where "Coyote took the form of a bird". The site is taken down, and it is discovered that many of the original posts were made by the teenage daughter of a former member of the Chaos Insurgency of Kootenai descent.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The Foundation deals with a metanarrative SCP and gets hoodwinked. The Chaos Insurgency gets involved.

Additional Notes: The most important thing I want to watch out for is that I don't mis-portray parts of any Native American culture(s). That being said, this very much isn't the mythical figure of Coyote as an SCP (that'd be both stupid and impossible to write), but is a conscious set of stories which act similar to the character they portray. The point is to look at how the foundation will handle an SCP like this, and vice versa…

item.title: Hikikomori
item.description: Seeking greenlight for an already written draft about a hikikomori that becomes a SCP object.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror, Drama/Emotional

Page Layout (Optional): Tabs for different security levels, each with different Special Containment Procedures. Clickable subsections within.

Elevator Pitch: A hikikomori ends up as a SCP entity by means of apparent suicide, becoming capable of entering reality from other people's dreams. Except that by doing so, he just discovered something very wrong about our reality.

Central Narrative: The ability to enter reality turns out to not be just a gimmick. Like the plot twist in the film "The Others", the roles are flipped: the SCP entity is more real that our waking life. Turns out that the SCP Foundation is protecting the waking reality itself by keeping that very secret. One of the things to do is to prevent real human contact with the hikikomori.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The story uses a similar layered security format as SCP-2718. Accurate information about the SCP and the very existence of that information turns out to be what is being contained, besides the entity itself.

Additional Notes: I already have a complete draft ready. The article links to SCP-2718 and SCP-2000, which are significant inspirations. However, this is a more traditional SCP article that doesn't in any way attempt to copy those two, and lacks the sort of semirealistic narrative as used in SCP-2817. I did not want to link this to the Oneiroi lore, and generally there are very few links to other SCPs.

item.title: Suicide Spore
item.description: Friendly SCP with a deadly disease.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.
Page type: SCP Article.
Elevator Pitch: An SCP that is friendly and compliant with containment, and will change its looks and actions to suit the observer best (it is an empathetic metamorph). There is a catch, though - any creature that has been in contact with it for an extended period of time will develop worrying symptoms that inclde an evental suicide, and these subjects are capable of indirectly spreading this "disease" (SCP-XXXX-2).
Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX is a friendly anomaly, found by the foundation after recieving reports of unnatural high suicide rates in North-West London. It was compliant with containment and is happy to stay isolated to guarantee the safety of others, thogh it is often reported to seem lonely and openly express this. However, it willingly stays in containment as to not endanger any more lives. It has often stated that it thinks SCP-XXXX-2 is the problem, and that it is simply infected with it, but research cannot be made of the matter.
Hook/Attention-Grabber: This is something I would need help with. Personally I think that the SCP willingly being contained without any special requests is interesting enough - I haven't seen any sentient SCPs that are willingly contained to save human lives. If you can find one please tell me, I'd love to read one.
Additional Notes: I do have a sandbox with a basic draft for this, but I'm afraid it's pretty poorly-written in my opinion.

Please tell me if I have missed any rules or anything, or if I have done this completely wrong.

item.title: SCP-XXXX
item.description: What do you think of that idea ?
item.content:encoded:
Hello there. So I had this idea of a bedroom. It doesn't look abnormal at first glance. However, when one walk inside, they will enter a state of euphoria, giggling for no apparent reasons. When they do this, they are designated as SCP-XXX-A. Once in that euphoric state, they will grab as many pillows as they can find in the room, and exit it. They will then run around, looking for a human being. Then, once they found one, they will throw a pillow at the person and start a pillow fight with them. The "target" will be designated as SCP-XXX-B. If SCP-XXX-B catches the pillow, they will enter the same state of euphoria and fight back with the pillow. Once the fight is done, SCP-XXX-A will go back to looking for another human being to "contaminate", and SCP-XXX-B will do the same.

However, if the target doesn't catch the pillow, they will not enter the euphoric state, and SCP-XXX-A will be discontent, trying to throw it back at SCP-XXX-B until they catch it. If someone stays with SCP-XXX-A in the same room for around 10 minutes, they will enter the state of euphoria, even if they didn't catch the pillow, and the room they were in takes the same abnormal properties as the original SCP-XXXX.

Once contaminated, SCP-XXX-A will never leave that euphoric state and must be terminated.

Keter or Euclide class. I was thinking of calling it "The Best Slumber Party Ever".

What do you think ? Has something similar already been done ?

item.title: Dr Cheese SCP idea.
item.description: My new Proposal for an SCP. Might be really bad (again) but I enjoyed it :)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article.

Genre: My design is meant to be spooky, but I may not achieve this factor.

Page Layout: The usual SCP statements, Item Name, Item Class but no picture. Information is going to be structured in the following layout; Appearance description (Height, weight, colour and shape), Discovery (How the anomaly was contained), Abilities (What the anomaly can do, how it does it etc) and the Addendums (Stories about previously explained things).

Elevator Pitch: The basic premise is a tall, slender, arctic hunter with elongated shoulder growths and large elbows, glowing crimson eyes, capable of seeing infrared radiation and heat signatures. This is used as a hunting technique in the arctic weather.

+ show block
– hide block

The anomaly has thousands of tiny muscles on its skin capable of moving guanine crystals to adjust the wavelength of light being reflected off the skin of the anomaly. This is commonly known as camouflage, and is the same method that the Chamaeleonidae (Common Chameleon) uses. Bone marrow scans and nervous axon scans have suggested that overgrowths on the anomaly's shoulder blades and elbows contain many nerve endings, which transfer electrical signals in large amounts to a particular area which creates an electromagnetic field. These electromagnetic pulses disrupt nearby local electric signals. It may use this to alter the function of electrical signals in the brain, or to inhibit power of technology.

Central Narrative: The narrative for initial containment is the following: It was a normal day in the UK Arctic Research Facility. Cold, as usual, but the sacred electric heaters were keeping staff alive. It was collection day, where the scientific staff would take a collection of snow for carbon-testing, a process where the amount of carbon that is in a snowflake is collected to see the effects of the greenhouse effect. As the staff left the facility, the power went out. As the staff stumbled over to the generator, senior researcher Noel Leon noticed a small red glow. Must have been nothing. H got back to fixing the generator. The fuses had been replaced. They become brittle and break in the cold weather. But as soon as the generator start-up was initiated, the generator failed. What was going on? Suddenly, pat… pat… pat…. Something was behind him, but when he turned around, there was nothing but footprints. SNAP. The crunch of his bones in SCP-XXXX's mouth was horrifying, but unheard to remaining staff. As it entered the facility, seven of it's prey had already been frozen. An easy meal. Junior researcher Doctor Edward turned a corner, but the anomaly was gone, just a frozen, half-eaten corpse. The rest of the facility was wiped out, with the exception of Doctor Bradly was obliterated by SCP-XXXX. Doctor Bradly called local authorities and the foundation was alerted. MTF unit Delta-92 Snow-and-Tell was sent to the situation and captured the anomaly.

item.title: My Idea for an SCP
item.description: SCP-6134 The Judge good ore evil?
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional)

Elevator Pitch: SCP-6134 is an anomaly that can appear behind someone who has done great evil. Then one year later that person reappears, either dead or alive. It is currently not captured. It cannot be captured by camera.

Central Narrative: A report by a civilian family reched the foundation, that is when investigations startet. Some years later a doctor of the foundation saw SCP-6134 live in action. Over the years many civilian have been asked about SCP-6134, all answered the same: " It is a black figure."

item.title: SCP Idea: Home is where the mind is.
item.description: A house that changes it’s inside
item.content:encoded:
A house that changes it’s inside, depending on the mentality of whoever’s living within it. (Need criticism and help for Greenlight!)

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Psychological Horror, Weird, Mixed Genres

Elevator Pitch: The basic concept is a singular home that changes the inside of itself physically to reflect the current mental state of whoever is living inside it. When first entering the home, it’s exactly the same for every person (Just a normal middle-class home with nothing strange.) Once the person becomes accommodated to the house (feels comfortable calling it their own home), that’s when the house begins to slowly change over time. (I’ll go through some small examples later on) The house mainly focuses on the subconscious/repressed thoughts and current temperament. The house itself isn’t inherently malicious, or has any goal. It simply just does what it does.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: The plan is to have the foundation do research on the house using a number of different D-class personnel with varying different backgrounds and personalities. My main vision for this SCP is having about 5-7 different experiment logs, each with a different outcome of what happens. It’ll begin with a brief description and background of the house’s current subject, before logging and explaining all the changes caught on camera/ told by the subject. A sort of list that I came up with lists the general mood I want from each section
1. normal interaction (Not too boring as to bore the reader, but some strange stuff happens)
2. cute interaction (A test on an animal, such as a dog. This is to lul the reader into a false sense of security)
3. weird interaction (More abstract things happen around the house.)
4. emotional interaction (This one I’m not so sure on, but it could be about a dead relative, or something similar)
5. really weird interaction (Things get far more intense and abstract, and may see how people start disappearing within the home.)
6. scary interaction (Straight up physical horror)
7. [REDACTED] (straight up unexplainable/eldritch horror type stuff.
Hook/Attention-Grabber: I hope the main hook of this SCP to audiences is having them wonder “What would the house do for me?” due to the house having a completely different experience to whomever enters it.

Additional Notes:
Examples:
A woman with claustrophobia slowly gets trapped inside the house.

An optimistic/life loving man becomes obsessed with the house and refuses to leave.

I'd love to know what everyone thinks/what I can do to improve this SCP! :)

item.title: [Feedback request] Enigma Dilemma
item.description: Some weapons of war become more dangerous as centuries pass.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Unsure, guidance requested

Elevator Pitch: An 18th century naval war table that displays the location of every military vessel currently on water in the world.

Central Narrative: The war table is suspected to have been made during the American Revolution*, leading to many of the naval battles of the war ending in British defeat despite their superiority on sea. It is also thought to have been used in the battles of Manila Bay (1898) and Coronel (1914), as well as many decisive (and unlikely) engagements in WWII. Following the war, the object was considered displaced and eventually lost until resurfacing in the continental US some 50 years later. Through unclear means, it had ended up in an antique shop where its outrageous price had scared off any buyers for years until the Foundation's involvement.

*the nature of the Battle of Quiberon Bay in 1759 has raised concerns regarding the object's assumed creation date.

+ show block
– hide block

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The title of this thread: an Enigma dilemma. In WWII, Britain cracked the Enigma cipher. However, using this to save every Allied naval convoy from U-boats would have made it obvious to the Germans that their cipher has been cracked, and so Allied command was faced with a question: you know where, what, and when the enemy will strike. Which attacks do you let happen and which attacks do you thwart?

This SCP is a similar question but on a far larger scale; every public, secret, and clandestine naval movement is laid bare. Any naval force secretly moving against another would force the international, humanity-shielding Foundation to either pick sides, or let conflict after conflict happen. With what could happen if it fell into the wrong hands, and with GOIs interested in acquiring the object, securing, containing, and protecting is very literal.

Additional Notes: This would be my first contribution to the site and as such, I would appreciate thorough criticism. There are currently no drafts and I am not counting on this being approved or greenlit, though that would be a nice surprise. Additionally, I'd like some help with the genres—or is History alone enough?

item.title: "God Bless Americana Anómalos" Idea Critique Request
item.description: The American Flag was a plant all along.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout:

  • ConProcs
  • Description
  • Discovery Log
  • List of SCP-Events
  • Testing Logs
  • Interview and Final Word from O5

Elevator Pitch:

You're home alone, watching the tv of your country. You hear a noise in the other room and go to investigate. You see nothing but the American flag planted firmly in the center of the room.

Then a voice whispers to you

"God bless America".

And then you start a revolution.

-Marcelles_Raynes 12/4/2020

1 out of every 5,000 American flags is a sentient petal of an extra-dimensional plant that symbiotically infects humans (mostly foreigners) and puppets them into influencing the political state of America with non-anomalous memetic strategies.

Story and Hook +
Story and Hook -

Central Narrative: The first American flag, the original progenitor of this SCP, inspired the American Revolution only because the east coast was the perfect habitat for it to grow. The anomaly successfully thrived in America for centuries undetected, keeping their percentage of American hosts lower than the percentage of non-American hosts globally. And while these flags are too light to stop the wind from pushing them around outside, inside the human body they can morph themselves into microscopic threads to navigate, manipulate their hosts, and avoid detection.

It isn’t until 2015, when the Bundy standoff between the BLM and the ATF revealed a new progenitor flag attempting to start another revolution, that the Foundation identifies the presence of the anomaly. While the Foundation realizes complete containment of the anomaly would force them and the US into open war, they also discover that the anomaly has been defending humanity from numerous shape-shifting anomalies in secret, making itself essential to their needs too. They accept that the anomaly cannot and does not need to be actively contained, so, with caution, they focus on the threat of wild American flags going rogue and starting a new America all over again.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Inspired by a comment made by Marcelles_Raynes 's perspective on the phrase “God Bless America,” this SCP focuses on highlighting and mocking much of American flavored jingoism while not explaining it all off as something completely unnatural.

Johnny Appleseed, tea dumping in the Boston river, the start of the Spanish-American war, Westerns, and others are given are both humorous and unsettling examples. Test logs show how flags choose/infect their host and how infected hosts take down other shape-shifting threats (hint: think of a "pulling a handkerchief out of the mouth" magic trick but deadly.) Also hints at the end about what might have O5 worried most of all about the anomalies freedom.

Additional Notes: The title is supposed to be the genus and species name but correct me if I got the order or idea wrong. Thanks!

item.title: Looking for Greenlight on fungal SCP
item.description: Infectious disease anomaly with what I believe to be a unique twist on the topic.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout:
Containment Procedures. There will be two sections - Original Containment and Revised Containment Procedures.
Description.
Addendums. Consists of short emails, lab reports, and mission transcripts. Will be how the “meat” of the narrative is told by leading the reader along a trail of breadcrumbs.

Elevator Pitch:
SCP-XXXX is a collective term for a genus of Glomeromycota (soil-borne fungi). A type of endoparasite only found in remote, humid environments within the latitudes of 23.5 N(Tropic of Cancer) and 23.5 S (Tropic of Capricorn), it infects organisms belonging to the order of Primates.

SCP-XXXX-1a refers to organisms infected with SCP-XXXX spores. Instances go through 3 stages of infection and are considered “mature” once they enter the fourth. Mature instances can reproduce SCP-XXXX by releasing spores. Has significant regenerational properties of interest to the Foundation as a result of SCP-XXXX “grafting” plant onto animal cells as it takes over the hosts’ body.

+ show block
– hide block

SCP-XXXX-1b refers to cocoons of inactive 1a instances. Since 1a instances use sunlight to metabolize ATP (which are essentially walking plants made of fungi), they enter a sort of hibernation when deprived of it by encasing themselves in calcified plant matter. If left for too long become 1c instances.

SCP-XXXX-1c instances are large fungal umbrella shaped bodies approximately three (3) meters in height and bioluminescent in color. The majority of its surface is covered in microscopic cilia specialized in capturing fungal spores from its immediate atmosphere. Furthermore, SCP-XXXX-1c is capable of accelerating abnormal amounts of fungal growth in its vicinity, creating entirely new ecosystems of toxic bioluminescent fungi. These new environments are referred to as SCP-XXXX-1d. SCP-XXXX spores are common around 1c and throughout 1d.

Bioluminescent fungi in SCP-XXXX-1d emit a fruity aroma that compels the victim to consume it. This effect is exponential over long periods of time, therefore classifying 1c and 1d instances as cognitohazards. Once ingested orally, victims fall into a coma, making them susceptible to infection via SCP-XXXX-1a instances

Central Narrative:
The Foundation tries to study an anomaly that could have medical benefits for personnel on the field if thoroughly understood. The site director, assigned to study the anomaly after recent failures in his own work, sees this as a chance to make his comeback. However, he, in in his pursuit to do so, unknowingly forces the anomaly through “artificial selection” (a process in which humans breed animals/plants in order to obtain offspring with certain traits), making the anomaly in general much more dangerous and difficult to contain than it originally was.

Hook/Attention Grabber: Humans make mistakes. We misjudge things which, ultimately, may end up making the situation worse. The Foundation is, at least partly, run by humans, and is therefore not exempt from this fact.

item.title: Harrowing Haberdashery
item.description: A sewing needle that transfer negative emotions to garments
item.content:encoded:
A sewing needle that transfer negative emotions to garments, which in turn magnify and transfer them to the wearer.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Page Layout (Optional): n/a

Elevator Pitch: Any instance of an otherwise ordinary sewing needle that transfers the negative thoughts and emotions of the user into the garment/item the needle is used to make or repair, but only when the the person sewing pricks their finger with the needle and draws blood. The garment/item then imparts those same negative thoughts and emotions, magnified several times over, into the end user of the created item. Items created with the needle retain those properties indefinitely, and have the ability to impart the same properties of the original needle onto any new needle that is used to alter or repair them, again with the requirement that the person using the needle pricks their finger and draws blood.

Central Narrative: From a story perspective, I plan for the article to contain incident reports with references to various historical events, with pieces of clothing of key participants in those events having been affected by the needle.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Has the ability to self propagate, though only under specific circumstances. This prevents it from being overpowered, while allowing instances to remain hidden in plain site for extended periods of time. The same applies to any items created with the needle, leading to sporadic “outbreaks” of items created with instances of the needle that must be responded to by the Foundation.

Additional Notes: n/a

item.title: (Looking for greenlight) Ancient elevators
item.description: Historical anomaly in which the electric elevator originates from 3000 BC
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Comedy / Bizarre (if that counts as a category)

Elevator Pitch:

  • According to the public, the elevator was invented and popularized in the late 1800's.
  • In actuality, the first elevators popped up around 3000 BC.
  • Functional elevators can be found in historic buildings; there's even ancient Egyptian elevators in the great pyramids.

Central Narrative:
The containment procedures and description serve to introduce the anomaly and explain how the Foundation is handling it. The Foundation puts out the story that the first elevator was installed in 1880, and whenever they find an elevator created before that date, they either destroy it, conceal it, or make it look like a modern elevator. It also serves to justify some aspects of the anomaly, like how elevators could be invented before electricity, or how knowledge of how to build an elevator could propagate in the first place.

+ show block
– hide block

Then there's an addendum explaining some notable examples of ancient elevators, which serve both to clarify the anomaly further and act as their own interesting anecdotes. Examples I have in mind are solid stone elevators installed into the great pyramids, how elevators are used in various medieval castles, and possibly even mentions of elevators in the bible.

The resolution to the SCP comes in the form of an MTF log. Foundation satellites detect an object manifest in space and slowly descend to the earth's surface. An MTF squad is deployed to the estimated landing zone, and discover it to be a descending elevator. When it hits the surface, aliens pop out, and explain that 4000 yeas ago, they gave the gift of elevators to man, having misinterpreted instructions from the alien queen to "uplift" our species.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
It might be ambitious for a first SCP, but if I go with the "aliens taught us how to make elevators" story, the hook could be that the object class is Explained, with the subclass of Keter, since even though the anomaly is explained the phenomenon still requires coverup procedures.

Alternatively, the hook could just be an incredibly jarring phrase in the containment procedures, like "Highly visible elevators installed in notable historic sites, such as the main lobby elevator of the Great Pyramid of Giza…".

Additional Notes:
Some of my favorite SCPs are the ones that are just about something straight up bizarre, like 5940 or 5319 or 2598 or 4062. Something about them appeals to me in a huge way, more than horror or drama ever does in SCPs. It's definitely what I wanna try for my first SCP, if it wouldn't be too much of a challenge.

item.title: The Recursive Dollhouse
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Fridge Horror/Emotional

Elevator Pitch: Essentially, SCP-XXXX a dollhouse of whatever environment it is currently being contained within. Likewise, it would sustain a diminished capability of whatever building it is housed in. SCP-XXXX-1 are essentially "dolls" housed in the facility that make up sentient/concious organisms. This also applies to anomalous materials as well, such as me, the toaster that speaks in the first person or the mask SCP. In addition, the anomalous effects of objects are still maintained but to a much smaller degree. Objects within the SCP-XXXX move in tandem with their current reality counterparts. Actions made within the main facility are mirrored in SCP-XXXX. There is in fact a miniature version of SCP-XXXX (dubbed SCP-XXXXa) and it is theorized that there are multiple versions of SCP-XXXX that exist within the dimensional realm.

Central Narrative: The SCP Foundation found this dollhouse in the middle of a nursery amongst other toys. After examining this, an entity attempts to contact them (potentially, though I am not sold on the concept) in an attempt to get it back.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The inherent dread of a recursive universe where what we view from within could in fact be caused by an upper plane of existence is terrifying, no?

Additional Notes: Edit 1: As for what happens when objects or instances of SCP-XXXX-1 are affected by outside users, I'd like to go into that further within test logs potentially. If not, essentially, the-what I dub-"dollhouse reality" can be affected by users. The current reality would be marginally affected in a similar manner. This isn't compulsory, however, but it does bring about satisfaction of the affected individual to complete said task. Other more violent actions such as the destruction of an instance of SCP-XXXX-1 can cause a severely minimized effect on the affected individual.If an anomalous SCP-XXXX-1 instance comes in contact with a non-anomalous instance of SCP-XXXX-1, the effects that would be generated by the anomalous instance are greatly minimized. Objects brought into the SCP-XXXX reality will manifest in the current reality as well.

item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) 'In Your Dreams: An instructional video on how to get the best sleep possible'
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Psychological Horror

Page Layout (Optional): More or less a traditional SCP article, though I plan to include a transcript of the tape and test results of those who viewed the tape.

Elevator Pitch: This SCP takes the form of a video tape. It is labelled 'In Your Dreams: an instructional video on how to get the best sleep possible' It starts out as a sleep instructional video before descending into madness, including subliminal messaging. The contents of the tape lead to massive psychological effects on whoever views the whole thing.

Central Narrative: The tape was discovered in the home of a suicide victim. The individual had no psychological issues prior to the viewing of the tape, which caught the attention of the SCP foundation. Attempts to find any info on the tape's origin has proven unsuccessful. However, the foundation has discovered multiple cases of homicides and suicides linked to this tape. All of the people who have viewed the tape and comply with all of its instructions suffer from insomnia, delusions, prone to self harm, sociopathic tendencies, and decreased empathy/compassion. Some extreme cases include incoherent rambling, and repeating the phrase "THERE ARE NO FACES."

In one incident, a copy of the tape was reportedly aired on TV in Mason County, Washington. Those who viewed the tape have received Class A amnesiacs, which have been proven successful with reversing the tapes effects

Hook/Attention-Grabber: There will be a disclaimer on the top stating that any staff who view the tape will be subject to Class A amnesiacs and an emergency psychological evaluation and that any unauthorized viewing of the tape will lead to termination, and any attempts at distributing the tape will lead to termination or reassignment to D-class.

Additional Notes: This was inspired by Local58's "real sleep". Honestly, the whole series is SCP material.

It helps them along, allows them to remember things better, formulate ideas faster, etc. After a while, it will take the form of a humanoid hallucination, engaging in long conversations with the victim. The victim becomes more and more detached from reality, spiraling into ritual and insanity as the "muse" takes over more and more of their mind, eventually taking full control of their body.

Central Narrative: A small foundation site collapses as the head researcher comes under the effect of the Muse.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The reveal of the muse not being a figment of the victim's mind but rather an independent entity.

Additional Notes: I think this could either turn out very good and interesting or very cliché.

item.title: Parasitic Amoeba
item.description: An Amoeba that is really fast and attacks the heart.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX Is a species of omnivorous amoeba that travel extremely fast throughout liquids and can terminate any organism in seconds.

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX-1 usually appears to those who have a small paycheck and have ease of access to a large container for water. Then SCP-XXXX-1 will dump a colony of SCP-XXXX into said container when the owner is near it. After dumping the colony the owner of the container will be frozen in place while SCP-XXXX walks towards and eventually into them, tell them to take care of the colony and then de-manifest.

Attention Grabber: I feel like there are a lot of SCPs that are either monstrous, cute or funny. But not all SCPs have to be that way. Another thing is that one thing goes through my head every time I hear of a K-Class end of the world scenario, that the world can be ended by something as big as a meteor or something as small as a micro-organism. I feel like there aren't enough small organisms in foundation custody that are capable of causing such an event.
